title: Bullying scenarios
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y8 lesson 1 (Bullying scenarios (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 1: Bullying, prejudice and being an upstander. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Prejudice and bullying
points: Prejudice: unfair views about a group

blocks.h: Is it bullying? (repeated, on purpose, a power imbalance)

questions.q: Two pupils argue once about a game and both say unkind things, then make up.
questions.a: Not bullying: a one-off falling out between equals. Upstander: help them calm down.

questions.q: For three weeks, a group leaves one pupil out of every breakout room and laughs when they speak.
questions.a: Bullying: repeated, deliberate, group against one. Upstander: invite them in, tell the teacher.

questions.q: Someone keeps sharing edited pictures of a classmate's work to mock it in a group chat.
questions.a: Bullying (online, repeated). Upstander: do not share or react; screenshot and report to a trusted adult.

questions.q: A pupil is called names every day because of their accent.
questions.a: Bullying, and prejudice-based. Upstander: say 'That's not OK', support the pupil, report it.

keywords.def: repeated, deliberate hurtful behaviour where there is an imbalance of power
an unfair opinion formed without reason or knowledge
someone who sees but does nothing
someone who acts safely to help

questions.q: Is this bullying? A one-off joke someone found upsetting.
questions.a: Not bullying on its own (not repeated), but still unkind; apologise.

questions.q: Core: Scenarios (pupil PDF): decide if each is bullying and write an upstander action.
Extend: In the portal response box, write a short message to support a target of bullying.
questions.a: 'I saw what happened. It was not okay. I have told a teacher; you are not alone.'

questions.q: Stretch: Explain how the Equality Act 2010 and the hadith 'help your brother' both oppose prejudice-based bullying.
questions.a: The law protects characteristics like race and religion; the hadith commands stopping wrongdoing.

questions.q: Which is the safest upstander action in a group chat?
options: Screenshot, message the target kindly, tell an adult
questions.a: B) Screenshot, message the target kindly, tell an adult. It supports the target and lets adults act, without escalating.

questions.q: Bullying is... A) one argument B) repeated, deliberate, with a power imbalance C) any disagreement
questions.a: B) repeated, deliberate, with a power imbalance
options: Repeated, deliberate, with a power imbalance

questions.q: Big question: if you watch bullying and say nothing, are you part of it? Explain.
questions.a: Silence can encourage it; a safe upstander action helps stop it.
